CFML Language Reference: Functions

CreateTimeSpan

Converts days, hours, minutes and seconds into a single number of days, including the fraction. Add it to a date, or pass it to the CACHEDWITHIN attribute of CFQUERY or the timeout attributes of CFAPPLICATION.

Category

Date and time functions

Syntax

CreateTimeSpan(days, hours, minutes, seconds)

Parameters

days
Number of days.
hours
Number of hours.
minutes
Number of minutes.
seconds
Number of seconds.

Returns

A number: the length of the span in days. CreateTimeSpan(0, 6, 0, 0) is 0.25.

Usage

All four arguments are required, even if they are zero. Values need not stay in their usual ranges: CreateTimeSpan(0, 0, 90, 0) is simply an hour and a half.

Adding a time span to a date gives a plain number of days rather than a date/time value, so wrap the sum in DateFormat/TimeFormat (or CreateODBCDateTime) before you show it.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Span = CreateTimeSpan(0, 6, 0, 0)>
<CFSET Start = CreateDateTime(1999, 12, 31, 20, 0, 0)>
<CFSET Finish = Start + Span>
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TD>CreateTimeSpan(0, 6, 0, 0)</TD><TD>#Span# days</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>CreateTimeSpan(1, 12, 0, 0)</TD><TD>#CreateTimeSpan(1, 12, 0, 0)# days</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Party starts</TD><TD>#DateFormat(Start, "mmm d, yyyy")# #TimeFormat(Start, "h:mm tt")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Plus six hours</TD><TD>#DateFormat(Finish, "mmm d, yyyy")# #TimeFormat(Finish, "h:mm tt")#</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
</CFOUTPUT>
<!--- Cache this query for 15 minutes --->
<CFQUERY NAME="Depts" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets" CACHEDWITHIN="#CreateTimeSpan(0, 0, 15, 0)#">
SELECT Dept_Name FROM Departments
</CFQUERY>
<CFOUTPUT><P>#Depts.RecordCount# departments, cached for 15 minutes.</P></CFOUTPUT>
